condition: Giant Cell Tumor of Tendon Sheath
indication_tracked: Romvimza is indicated for treatment of adult patients with symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumour (TGCT) associated with clinically relevant physical function deterioration and in whom surgical options have been exhausted or would induce unacceptable morbidity or disability.
indication_source: Therapeutic indication as published in EMA's medicines data (word for word)

eu.epar_summary:
Romvimza is a medicine used to treat adults with symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumour (TGCT); it is used in people with TGCT who have serious movement limitations and for whom surgery is no longer an option or would cause serious long-term problems.

TGCT is a condition where a non-cancerous tumour develops around a joint and tendons and can damage surrounding tissues. It usually affects a single joint, most often the knee or ankle of young and middle-aged adults. Symptoms usually include pain, swelling, stiffness and difficulty moving the joint.

TGCT is rare, and Romvimza was designated an ‘orphan medicine’ (a medicine used in rare diseases) on 16 December 2019.

Romvimza contains the active substance vimseltinib.
